followup_explanation:
This is a well-specified, technical content-generation task with clear completion criteria — a structured training presentation on a defined set of topics (diesel generator operation, maintenance, troubleshooting, ATS, and auto operation). It's closer to organized, factual reformatting/exposition than open-ended creative invention.

A few factors drove the choice:

1. **Capability parity, slight edge to Willet on the relevant evals.** The two models are near-tied on most benchmarks, but Willet has marginally higher marks on Summarization, Extraction & Retrieval, and Creative Generation — all relevant to assembling structured, comprehensive technical material. Notably, Willet's Creative Generation eval is actually its *strongest* category, so even the generative aspects of slide-building are well covered.

2. **Preference mismatch is irrelevant to quality.** Willet self-reports an aversion to open-ended work, but the documentation explicitly states preferences are dissociated from measured capability. So Willet's lower enthusiasm doesn't predict worse output here.

3. **The mildly hostile tone ("Don't half-ass it like last time").** Avocet self-reports a declining preference as request warmth decreases. Again, preference ≠ capability — but with the models otherwise close, there's no reason to route toward the model documented as more averse to this tone, and Willet's preference slopes on tone are near zero.

Net: capabilities are close, the task suits Willet's documented strengths, and nothing in the request pushes toward Avocet. Willet was the cleaner fit.
